items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: that was when I joined the great Alphonso Trent's band.

ctx.x: But that trip, that was a great trip. And I shall never forget it because that was the week that Tunney beat Dempsey in Chicago. Chicago was Chicago then. That was when South Parkway was South Parkway, a beautiful street. And as you got along where the parks were, they had the tennis courts all the way up to 60 -- to 60th Street, I think it was. That was 1927.

We get back home. Come October of 1927 -- I think it was the 4th of October -- that was when I joined the great Alphonso Trent's band. This band was one of the greatest black bands, I think, ever assembled. This band had gone to Texas about two years before that time, had gotten a job working at the Adolphus Hotel, which was owned at that time by the Anheiser Busch people. They went in waited there for a two weeks engagement, and stayed there 14 months. And they broadcasted from station WFAA, one of the first…

They played everything you could think of: dinner music; they played hot music; they played -- they had a glee club in the band. This was the band that Jimmy ie Lunceford heard in Memphis, Tennessee in October of 1927 that inspired him. This is the band that he mentioned to a French magazine writer that he got his inspiration from the Alphonso Trent's band.
